Zero model modules under the Name-prefix rule and under tools/ladder.py's is_model rule (MODEL_LAYER = Causal.Minkowski, Causal.Static, Causal.SingularFlat, Causal.Flat, Causal.Model, Causal.Port). tools/ladder.py model_path('Causal.InextensiblePiece', lean_index()['imports']) is None. Causal.InextensiblePiece.content: 5 constants, all moved: the four theorems and the matcher inextensible_connectedComponentIn.match_1_1. collectAxioms gives propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound for each. Statements: an abstract Causality C on a topological space M, [T2Space M], an open W, curves ℝ → M, a continuous T : M → ℝ, IsOpen/IsLUB/IsGLB of a set of ℝ, connectedComponentIn (ℓ ⁻¹' W) t, IsCauchySurfaceOn. No metric notion in any statement; the proofs use the metric of ℝ only (Metric.isOpen_iff, balls of ℝ). The docstring quotes def:cauchy_surface (ETT.tex:999-1000), marks no label, gives a hypothesis checklist for inextensible_connectedComponentIn, and in SCOPE records the verbatim hoist (with line ranges), why Causal.LadderLocal is imported, and the sibling left in Causal.Model.EAlphaCauchy.
Causal.InextensiblePiece.why_ladderlocal: Causal.Inextensible and Causal.Cauchy hold every notion the four theorems use, but with `import Causal.Cauchy` alone the module does not elaborate: `hO.connectedComponentIn` (inextensible_connectedComponentIn, now :183) fails with 'failed to synthesize LocallyConnectedSpace ℝ'. In QuasilinearOneSided's closure that instance was found as instLocallyConnectedSpace ∘ LocallyConvexSpace.toLocPathConnectedSpace ∘ NormedSpace.toLocallyConvexSpace ∘ InnerProductSpace.toNormedSpace ∘ RCLike.toInnerProductSpaceReal, with ContinuousSMul ℝ ℝ from IsModuleTopology.toContinuousSMul ∘ IsTopologicalSemiring.toIsModuleTopology (the old term's constants, by module). Probes, each elaborating the module's text under a candidate import list and printing type and value hashes of the 5 constants. Calibration: under HEAD QuasilinearOneSided's own five imports the probe reproduces the 'before' dump hashes exactly. Results: Causal.Inextensible + Causal.Cauchy + Causal.LadderLocal: identical (all 5). Causal.Cauchy + Causal.CurveComponents, + Causal.NestedCausalities, + Causal.MeasureRemarks: identical. Causal.Cauchy + Causal.Measure: inextensible_connectedComponentIn differs (value 3510311563 against 1667507348). Causal.Cauchy + Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic + Mathlib.Analysis.LocallyConvex.WithSeminorms: inextensible_connectedComponentIn differs (2162750976), the ContinuousSMul ℝ ℝ argument going through ContinuousMul.to_continuousSMul. Adding Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Module.ModuleTopology to that list makes it identical. The three mathlib modules and LocPathConnected are in the closures of Causal.MeasureRemarks and Causal.LadderLocal (through MeasureRemarks's Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Real import) and not in those of Causal.Cauchy or Causal.Measure (probe). The evidence's set was kept: it is ETT-layer, it is the import set the target names, and it restores every proof term. Reading taken, flagged here: Causal.Cauchy + Causal.CurveComponents gives a smaller closure (22 Causal modules against 28) with the same terms, if the master prefers it.

Elaborate the moved text in a scratch file (imports plus the module body plus an #eval printing Expr.hash of each moved constant's type and value). Calibrate it first under the old file's own import list, where it must reproduce the dump. Here the narrowest notional closure (Causal.Cauchy) did not elaborate at all (LocallyConnectedSpace ℝ missing). A mathlib-only fix (InnerProductSpace.Basic + LocallyConvex.WithSeminorms) elaborated to a different term (ContinuousSMul ℝ ℝ through ContinuousMul.to_continuousSMul instead of IsModuleTopology), and only Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Module.ModuleTopology or an ETT module reaching Causal.MeasureRemarks restored the old one. Note that ConstantInfo.value? returns none for theorems unless allowOpaque := true (Lean v4.31.0, Lean/Declaration.lean:482).
notes: Strict-library refactor. No statement changed, no declaration disappeared, was renamed or was added. In QuasilinearOneSided's closure every moved constant has its old type, universes, telescope and proof term, and only its module changed (dump). For the master: (1) Root import, README rows and the kb/0081 update are in master_changes; no curation, binder or ladder change is needed. (2) Import set: the evidence's Causal.Inextensible, Causal.Cauchy, Causal.LadderLocal, verified to restore every proof term; Causal.Cauchy alone fails to elaborate. Causal.Cauchy + Causal.CurveComponents would do as well with a smaller closure (new_modules.why_ladderlocal), the master's call. (3) Reading taken in QuasilinearOneSided's docstring: the target statement T-loc-quasilinear-one-sided/3-inextensible-piece keeps its mark, with a sentence saying where the theorem now lives. The theorem is certified and in the module's import closure, but no longer declared in that file. No tool reads target labels from docstrings, and no ledger curates the name. If the master wants a mark to mean 'declared here', unmark it and move the label's mention to Causal.InextensiblePiece's docstring. (4) Causal.InextensiblePiece is a natural home for T-loc-ealpha-tidy's inextensible_Iio_of_tendsto_not_mem (the target's evidence). (5) No git command that writes was run. The scratch files are kept for the auditor in /tmp/hinx: the HEAD copy of the file and the cut block (head/), the dumps before_qos.tsv, after_qos.tsv, after_inx.tsv with .mods closure lists, their generator dump/DumpBody.lean + dump/mk.sh and the comparer dump/cmp.py, and the import probes (probe/try.sh, try_*.lean, h_*.tsv, consts_old.tsv).
